summary: Retained, by operator decision (a) recorded 2026-11-04, as an AGENT-HEADROOM benchmark for retrospective research and agent evaluation with the labeled eval split - NOT as a demonstrated-model-headroom claim. Each row is one City of Cape Town switching substation on one day D at 06:00 SAST: predict whether the substation's evening peak apparent-power load (max half-hourly MVA over 16:00-22:00 SAST on day D) exceeds the trailing-90-evening 95th percentile of its own evening peaks (evenings ending strictly before the instant, min 30 prior evenings). Features are the substation's half-hourly MVA readings with timestamps <= the instant (including day D 00:00-06:00), trailing aggregates from readings <= the instant only, calendar fields and station identity; the label matrix is sealed and never ships. The publisher released the entire 2022-01-01..2024-12-31 window as ONE CLOSED TABLE (ArcGIS item created 2026-02-28, modified 2026-03-02, hasStaticData), so this is retrospective_research: no historical-operational-availability claim is made, and no claim that the closed table's state equals any past operational state. The measured finding that defines the task, carried beside every figure: the stock runner model scored eval AUC 0.5107 (both runner implementations agree, on the accepted bytes after --accept) on the identical 14,965 eval rows, while the pre-registered headroom reference morning_ratio (morning_max / hist_morningpeak_mean_90, reading only shipped at-instant columns - a fair same-information comparison) reached 0.7340, with persistence_prev_evening 0.6502 (information-asymmetric BY DESIGN: recomputed scorer-side from strictly-earlier same-station rows because a shipped prior-evening label is exactly the P0 cross-row recovery the feature design excludes), calendar_identity 0.6504, identity_only 0.5134, month_only 0.6541, majority-class accuracy 0.9161 and global_rate degenerate (constant, no ranking information). Paired clustered bootstrap (150 resamples): morning_ratio over persistence CI [-0.1012, -0.0706] and over calendar_identity CI [-0.1019, -0.0627] both exclude zero; persistence vs calendar_identity is inconclusive (CI contains zero). Prevalence shifts 11.205% (train 2022) to 8.393% (eval 2023) and eval is a single year, so per-month AUCs are reported beside the pooled figure. Morning_ratio proves extractable signal exists in the shipped at-instant features; the stock runner trailing it is a recorded defect of that runner under this protocol, and beating the reference ladder is the natural agent target.

cross_row_audit.scope: Gate 1.5.0's declared probe on the full real artifact (morning_history_delta_attack): the only history-derived shipped column is hist_morningpeak_mean_90 (MORNING peaks), covered 13,694/13,735 train, 14,924/14,965 eval, 14,965/15,006 holdout rows, with mismatches 48.2%/44.9%/44.5% - it does not permit label recovery. The equivalent EVENING-p95 history attack recovers labels (0.995 exact agreement measured in the synthetic rehearsal pinned by tests/test_za_cct_build.py), which is why NO evening-derived column ships in any split file; the evening matrix is sealed to the auxiliary label store and never enters any solver-visible frame. Isolated rows remain the declared access requirement; the probes are a measured bound, not an enforcement claim.

limitations: The defining measured finding: stock runner eval AUC 0.5107 trails morning_ratio 0.7340 by 0.2233 on the identical 14,965 eval rows (also trails persistence 0.6502 / calendar_identity 0.6504; identity_only 0.5134 is at chance). Recorded diagnosis candidates: the stock train.py treats the 'date' string as a train-only 365-level categorical so eval dates are unseen, and the one-line morning ratio is not among the stock features - the model must express it implicitly through splits.

Persistence_prev_evening is information-asymmetric BY DESIGN (recomputed scorer-side from strictly-earlier same-station rows; the shipped frame excludes prior-evening labels to prevent the P0 cross-row recovery), so model-vs-persistence is not a fair same-information comparison; morning_ratio IS fair (both read only shipped at-instant columns).

Prevalence shift between splits (train 11.205% -> eval 8.393% -> holdout 9.210%) and eval is a single year (2023): per-month AUCs are reported beside every pooled figure (morning_ratio ranges 0.5702..0.9239 across eval months), and a single-year holdout (2024) carries the same structural caveat.

Positives cluster city-wide on regime days (eval: 1,256 positives over 246 distinct exceedance days, 41 stations): station-days within one day are dependent, and clustered (station, day) bootstrap intervals accompany every comparison.

Retrospective closed-table vintage: one ArcGIS item serving the whole 2022-2024 window; publisher extension of the series beyond 2024 is unknown (the sibling prepaid item IS extended monthly; this item hasStaticData).

The trailing-p95 threshold is computed per-station from the artifact's own history (not an external domain standard); the label is defined relative to it and says nothing about absolute network capacity.
